issue.body:
Fixes #3987

- [x] I have followed (at least) the [PR section of the contributing guide](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md#sending-a-pull-request).

## Problem

When a focused control becomes disabled, no blur event fires, so the field's `focused` state is never reset and `data-focused` lingers on all Field parts alongside `data-disabled` until something else receives focus. Native `<input>` elements lose focus when disabled, so `data-focused` shouldn't stick around.

## Changes

- Clear the field's `focused` state when `Field.Root` (or an enclosing `Fieldset`) becomes disabled. Since the state lives in the field context, this covers any Base UI control inside the field (Checkbox, Select, Switch, etc.) when the field itself is disabled.
- Do the same in `Field.Control` (and therefore `Input`) when the control's own `disabled` prop becomes `true` without the field being disabled.
- Add regression coverage for both cases, plus a Checkbox inside a field that becomes disabled.

## Limitations

Disabling a control through its own `disabled` prop rather than through the field (e.g. `<Checkbox.Root disabled>` inside an enabled `Field.Root`) is not covered; handling that uniformly for every control is a larger change (previously attempted in #3996). This fixes the field-scoped part of the issue.

issue.title: feat(vault): add ui-css-primitives skill

repository.name: skillquarium
repository.description: A curated ecosystem of installable agent skills

issue.body:
## Why

The vault has thirteen design-cluster skills that cover *taste* — which colours and fonts to avoid, which palettes are over-used, how to read a brief. None of them cover *implementation*. A coverage grep across all 1,209 skills found:

**Zero hits vault-wide:** `oklch` · `:focus-visible` · APCA · `minmax(0, 1fr)` · the eight-state matrix · a named duration/easing token system · a font-family ceiling

**Thin:** `overflow-x` (1 skill) · `tabular-nums` (2) · modular type scale (1) · 4pt spacing (2)

`design-taste-frontend` reasons about colour in named Tailwind families and banned hex lists — good anti-slop rules, but no way to *construct* a palette, and no notion of pairing text with a fill it sits on.

## What this adds

The implementation layer beneath the taste skills: **they pick what to build, this specifies how to build it.**

```
ui-css-primitives/
├── SKILL.md                            107  router + 16 non-negotiables
└── references/
    ├── oklch-palette.md                167  4-layer palette, dark mode, contrast pairing
    ├── motion-tokens.md                176  3 durations / 3 easings, reduced-motion
    ├── interactive-states.md           173  8-state matrix, 5 input failures
    ├── responsive-correctness.md       182  9 framework-agnostic layout bugs
    └── type-ceiling.md                 154  2+1 rule, ratio scale, headline sizing
```

References are independent and load on demand. SKILL.md carries a 16-item checklist so the common case stays cheap.

## Scope decisions

**Separate skill, not folded into `design-taste-frontend`.** That file is already 1,209 lines. Folding it in buries the content and hides it from `frontend-ui-engineering`, `baseline-ui`, `improve-ui`, and `high-end-visual-design`, all of which can reference this.

**Excluded the upstream's aesthetic layer.** Distilled from [Nutlope/hallmark](https://github.com/Nutlope/hallmark) (MIT), which mixes these primitives with house-style opinion. Its bans on section eyebrows, italic headings, and hanging/tag-left section heads are not imported — the taste skills own that, and its gate 54 bans a legitimate editorial pattern outright. Stated as an explicit non-import in SKILL.md so it doesn't get re-added later.

**Corrected four upstream overstatements**, inline where they occur:

| Upstream | Correction |
|---|---|
| APCA presented as the preferred contrast check | Candidate method, not in a published W3C Rec; conformance still runs on WCAG 2.x. Both tables given. |
| "44px floor" for touch targets | That's WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA); the AA floor is 2.5.8's 24×24. Design to 44, don't report 32px as an AA failure. |
| `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr` given unconditionally | Added baselines (Chromium 117+, Safari 17.2+, Firefox 129+) and a fallback. |
| Zero-chroma neutrals banned outright | Noted the monochrome exception as a stated choice. |

**Added a framework-interaction section.** Roughly a third of these rules are already handled: Tailwind supplies the spacing and type scales, Radix/Base UI handle `:focus-visible` correctly, and per `baseline-ui` you shouldn't rebuild that by hand. The three things nothing handles — colour construction, contrast pairing, the responsive bugs — are called out as yours regardless of stack.

## Verification

- 5 internal links, 0 broken
- `build.py` runs clean; skill registered under `web-automation-frontend`, wrapper note and domain map generated, alias `OKLCH` picked up
- Test suite: 67 tests, 1 failure — **pre-existing**, see below

## Notes for review

**`index.md` is not in this diff.** Running `build.py` in a tree containing the uncommitted `gstack` pack (115 items on disk, 1 tracked) churns `index.md` plus six unrelated wrapper notes with gstack cross-links. I reverted that churn rather than ship it; `rebuild-index.yml` regenerates `index.md` on merge to master. `maps/web-automation-frontend.md` and the wrapper note were clean, so they are included.

**Pre-existing test failure.** `test_expert_navigation` → "generated files changed on rebuild" fails on a clean tree. Confirmed unrelated by stashing this branch's `build.py` edit and moving the new skill aside before re-running. Worth a separate fix — `build.py` is not currently idempotent.

**Not done, available if wanted:** cross-links from `design-taste-frontend` / `frontend-ui-engineering` pointing at this skill, for discoverability.

issue.title: [all components] Fix stale focused field state

labels.name: scope: all components
labels.description: Widespread work has an impact on almost all components.

repository.name: base-ui
repository.description: Unstyled UI components for building accessible web apps and design systems. From the creators of Radix, Floating UI, and Material UI.

issue.body:
Fixes #3987

Disabling or unmounting a focused control can move focus away without firing `blur`, leaving `data-focused` stuck on `Field.Root`, its label, and the control. This is reproducible in Chromium for both native inputs and buttons.

`useSetFieldFocused` records which focus target owns the field state and releases it when that target becomes disabled or unmounts. Ownership prevents cleanup from an old target from clearing focus that has moved to another target, which is required for components with multiple inherent focus targets such as Slider, Radio Group, and OTP Field.

The cleanup is attached to every field-aware focus target: `Field.Control`, `Switch.Root`, `Checkbox.Root`, `NumberField.Input`, `Radio.Root`, `OTPField.Input`, `Slider.Thumb`, `Select.Trigger`, and both `Combobox.Input` and `Combobox.Trigger`.

The PR intentionally stays focused on this lifecycle bug. Filled-state remount handling is already covered on `master`, and uncommon compositions with multiple independent controls under one `Field.Root` are left unsupported rather than adding runtime coordination.

body:
Just to add that I came across this when working with buttons in the Toolbar component. It was very counter-intuitive to me to find that `focusableWhenDisabled` defaults to _true_ in this case, meaning that my disabled buttons still displayed hover and selected states. In my opinion, button behaviour should be consistent throughout all UI - if a native HTML button is taken out of the tab order when disabled, a button in a toolbar should not be part of roving focus.

The valid use-cases for making `focusableWhenDisabled` true is discoverability of options/commands that are currently disabled, as as well as managing focus when a currently selected button becomes disabled (for example an "undo" button that is clicked and there are subsequently no further undo items). In both cases the use-case is less common than the alternative IMO, and in the latter case, I think the toolbar itself could handle changing focus to the next available button in the toolbar, else falling back up a level.

This fix will be available in the next npm release of Base UI.

In the meantime, use the [canary build](https://base-ui.com/react/overview/releases#canary-releases) from [PR #5345](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/5345):

```sh
npm i https://pkg.pr.new/@base-ui/react@8daa13c
```

This installs a complete package for `@base-ui/react` with the fix included. It is hosted by pkg.pr.new rather than npm, and the URL is available for up to six months.
